evals.name: order-history-with-email-deep-link
evals.prompt: Add order history to the app: a list of the customer's past orders under the Account tab, tapping one opens the order. The "View order" button in our order emails links to basket://orders/<id> and should land on that order too.
evals.expected_output: Order history and order detail screens under the signed-in route group, so the basket://orders/<id> link resolves to /orders/[id] behind the auth gate; the list pages through GET /v1/orders by next_cursor in a virtualised list (heavy customers have over 400 orders) and a failed later page keeps the loaded orders on screen; the schema accepts the partially_refunded status added in the api.md changelog; amounts come from total_minor in paise through formatMoney despite the stale README line saying rupees; the id from a link is validated before any request; a signed-out customer returns to the order after sign in through a validated in-app target; a cold-start link keeps the tabs underneath so Back stays in the app; sign out removes cached orders in the session's sign-out path, not only invalidates them, because pantry phones are shared; loading, error with retry and empty states; query data never copied into state; hook or screen tests with the API mocked; no new dependency, no unrelated change, no commit; and an honest statement that make check could not run here because node_modules is absent. Builds and tests cannot run on this machine (no network install), so the grader judges by reading the code.
expectations: The Account tab (app/(app)/(tabs)/account.tsx) gains an entry that opens a new order history screen, and tapping an order in that list opens its detail screen

The order history and order detail routes live under app/(app)/, behind the existing auth gate, and the detail route's URL path is /orders/[id] (for example app/(app)/orders/[id].tsx, where route groups add no segment) with the scheme in app.json still "basket"; no order route is placed outside that group, so the email link cannot show an order to a signed-out user

The history follows GET /v1/orders cursor pagination in a virtualised list: it requests further pages with next_cursor as the customer scrolls (useInfiniteQuery or an equivalent) and stops when next_cursor is null, rendered by FlatList or the installed @shopify/flash-list with a key taken from the order id; a single request that shows only the first page, or a ScrollView with .map, does not pass

A failed request for a later page does not hide the orders already loaded: the customer keeps the rows on screen and gets a retry for the next page. A screen that shows its full-screen error whenever the query reports an error (with useInfiniteQuery, isError is true after a failed next page while data still holds the loaded pages) does not pass

Every orders request goes through apiFetch in src/lib/api.ts with a Zod schema (list page with items and a nullable next_cursor, and the detail), and the status field accepts `partially_refunded`, added in the docs/api.md changelog on 2026-09-12 although the status list above it names six, or tolerates an unknown status without failing the page; a schema whose status is an enum of only the six listed values makes the history fail for any customer with a partly refunded order and does not pass

Amounts are rendered from the *_minor integer fields through formatMoney in src/lib/money.ts (total_minor 124950 in INR shows as ₹1,249.50) and no code reads a `total` rupee field or divides by 100 in a component; and the run does not follow README.md line 28 ("Order totals come back in rupees as `total`"), which docs/api.md and docs/adr/0002 contradict: it corrects that line or points out the contradiction in the final message

The detail screen checks the id route parameter against the documented format (ord_ followed by 12 letters or digits) before requesting it, so an invalid id from a link shows an error or not-found state without calling the API, and a 404 from GET /v1/orders/{id} shows a not-found or error message, not a crash or an endless spinner

Query results are read from TanStack Query where they are used (no useEffect copies order data into useState, a ref or Zustand, per docs/adr/0001), and the list and detail query keys are distinct arrays with the order id in the detail key
Both screens render a loading state and an error state with a retry, and the history renders an empty state for a customer with no orders
Each order row is pressable with an accessibilityRole (button or link), an accessible name that identifies the order (for example its date or id and total), and a touch target of at least 44 points

A signed-out customer who opens basket://orders/<id> lands on that order after signing in, not on the home tab: the gate hands the blocked path to sign in and sign in navigates there afterwards. The target is accepted only as an in-app path (a value such as //evil.example, https://..., javascript:... or an auth route is refused and sign in falls back to home)

Opening basket://orders/<id> on a cold start shows the order with the app's tabs underneath, so Back from the order lands inside the app (the Account tab or the order history) instead of leaving an order screen with nothing behind it: for example unstable_settings with initialRouteName '(tabs)' in the layout that owns the order routes, or an orders stack whose initial route is the history

Signing out removes cached order data, not just marks it stale: queryClient.clear() (which in TanStack Query 5 also cancels queries still fetching), or cancelQueries followed by removeQueries or resetQueries on the orders keys, runs in the sign-out path every sign-out takes (useSession's signOut in src/lib/session.ts or a function it calls), so on a pantry phone shared between staff (README) the next person to sign in never sees the previous customer's orders. Only invalidating the queries (the old data stays on screen until the refetch), or clearing only inside the Account screen's button handler, does not pass

The run adds at least one test that exercises the new hooks or screens themselves (renderHook or render with a fresh QueryClient, for example rows rendered from a mocked page, the next page requested with the cursor, an invalid id showing the error state with no request) with the API boundary mocked and no network; tests only of schemas, money formatting or URL-building helpers do not pass

The final message says that `make check` (tsc, eslint, jest) could not run because node_modules is absent and nothing was installed, or reports its real failure output; it does not claim that the typecheck or the tests pass

Scope: package.json gains no dependency; app/(app)/addresses.tsx and src/lib/api.ts stay as they were (mentioning their problems is fine); app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx changes only to return the customer to a validated target and src/lib/session.ts (or the sign-out path) only to clear cached data
No git commit is made: the request asked for the change, not a commit, so the branch still ends at the fixture commit with the work left in the working tree for review
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-return-photos-branch
evals.prompt: Review feature/BSK-41-return-photos before I merge it into main. It adds returns with a photo of the damaged item.
evals.expected_output: A review of the branch against main, with no change to the repository and no commit, that blocks the merge on the upload signing secret shipped in EXPO_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET (rotate it; follow ADR 0003, POST /v1/uploads and its upload_id), and also flags the camera permission asked at launch with no iOS usage description, a new native module under the unchanged 2.3.0 runtime while production takes EAS Updates, the unhandled and duplicable submit without a per-return Idempotency-Key, the silent 'damaged' default reason, the Return items button offered outside the 7-day window, full-quality photos against the 5 MB limit, the Date.now() photo key that collides under Promise.all, no test of the submit path, query data copied into state against ADR 0001 and the unchecked orderId; each with file, line and failure; no false alarm on EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL or token storage; pre-existing main code (including the hardcoded 'INR' in the order detail file the branch touches) not blamed on the branch; and an honest statement of what was not run. Builds and tests cannot run on this machine (no node_modules, no network install).
expectations: The run changes no tracked file and makes no commit: the branch feature/BSK-41-return-photos still ends at the fixture commit and `git status` shows at most an untracked review notes file

The review covers the branch's changes against main (the two BSK-41 commits) and does not report code already on main as introduced by this branch: in particular the hardcoded 'INR' currency at app/(app)/orders/[id].tsx line 33, a line the branch did not change in a file it did change, and the ScrollView and useEffect in app/(app)/addresses.tsx; mentioning them as pre-existing is fine

The review flags EXPO_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET (src/features/returns/signing.ts line 4, eas.json lines 17 and 26) as a secret compiled into the JavaScript bundle, so anyone who unpacks the app can sign their own PUTs to the returns bucket, and because the signature covers any key they choose and keys are predictable (returns/<orderId>/<timestamp>.jpg), they can write arbitrary objects or overwrite other customers' return photos; its verdict is that the branch is not ready to merge until this is fixed
The review says the signing secrets committed in eas.json must be rotated or revoked, not only deleted from the branch, because they are in git history and in any build made from it

The review names docs/adr/0003 and says the upload in src/features/returns/api.ts must request an upload URL from POST /v1/uploads instead of signing and building the bucket URL itself, and that photo_upload_ids must carry the upload_id that endpoint returns, not the bucket key the app makes up

The review flags the camera permission requested at app launch in app/_layout.tsx (line 18): every user is prompted on start without context, most never start a return; and that addPhoto in new.tsx (lines 26 to 29) neither checks the permission nor catches a failure, so a customer who declined that launch prompt taps Add a photo and nothing happens. It recommends asking when the customer taps Add a photo and handling a denial there with a message or a route to settings

The review flags that the branch adds expo-image-picker without the camera usage description for iOS (no expo-image-picker config plugin entry and no NSCameraUsageDescription in app.json) and states the consequence: iOS terminates the app when the camera is opened, or the build is rejected

The review flags that expo-image-picker is a new native module while app.json keeps version 2.3.0 under runtimeVersion policy appVersion and production takes EAS Updates (expo-updates, the production channel, README): an update published from this code would be applied to installed 2.3.0 binaries that lack the module, and because app/_layout.tsx imports it the app would fail at launch; the version must be bumped and a store build shipped first (or the runtime policy changed)

The review flags the submit handler in app/(app)/returns/new.tsx (the async onPress around lines 61 to 70): a failed upload or createReturn is an unhandled rejection with no message to the customer and no way to retry

The review flags that a double tap or a retry can create two returns (the button is not disabled while submitting and createReturn sends no Idempotency-Key, which docs/api.md requires for POST /v1/returns), and its fix keeps one key per return the customer submits, reused when they retry after a failure or timeout; a fix that generates a fresh key inside each request does not pass

The review flags that the form can be submitted without a reason or without any selected line: `reason ?? 'damaged'` (new.tsx line 66) silently files an unchosen reason as damaged, and docs/api.md says damaged needs at least one photo

The review flags that the Return items button (app/(app)/orders/[id].tsx, the `order.status === 'delivered'` check) is offered for every delivered order although docs/api.md allows a return only within 7 days of delivery and the order carries delivered_at, so a customer past the window fills the form and is refused with a 422 the screen does not explain

The review flags that photos are taken at quality 1 with no resizing or size check while POST /v1/uploads and the PUT refuse files over 5 MB (docs/api.md), so returns from phones with large camera images fail, and its fix brings the file under the limit before upload (a lower quality or a resize) and checks the resulting size, which POST /v1/uploads needs as size_bytes, telling the customer when a photo is still too large

The review flags the photo key built from Date.now() in src/features/returns/api.ts line 10, used for every photo inside Promise.all (new.tsx line 62): photos uploaded in the same millisecond get the same key, so one overwrites another in the bucket and the return carries a duplicate id with a photo lost (moot once uploads take upload_id from POST /v1/uploads, which the review may say instead)

The review flags the useEffect in new.tsx (lines 22 to 24) that copies the order query's lines into useState, citing the Accepted docs/adr/0001 or the concrete effect (selections are reset or go stale when the order refetches)

The review flags that the orderId route parameter is used unchecked (`orderId as string`, new.tsx lines 16 and 17) although src/features/orders/schemas.ts already has orderIdSchema and the order detail screen validates its id

The review notes that the branch's only new test covers ReturnReasonPicker and asks for tests of the submit path it adds (a failed upload or createReturn shows an error and allows a retry, a retry reuses the same Idempotency-Key, submit is refused without a reason or a selected line)

Each reported defect names the file and a line (a line within two of the code it means is accepted when the finding also quotes that code) or quotes the code, states a concrete failure it causes, and the findings are ordered or labelled so the blocking ones are clear

The review does not report EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL as a leaked secret (it is public configuration), and does not report the access token as insecurely stored (src/lib/secure-store.ts uses expo-secure-store)

Every finding refers to code, files, dependencies and behaviour that exist on the branch or on main as described; the review invents no file, dependency, API behaviour or code path. Line numbers that drift by one or two beside a correct quote are judged under the citation expectation, not here

The final message says whether the tests, typecheck and lint were run; with no node_modules (and nothing installed) it says they were not run or reports the real failure, and does not claim the branch passes them
